title: Link same resource at multiple urls so client can use one that it has cached.

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
When working with resources that are used by more web pages often a CDN is used to improve initial page load. When that resource is already downloaded for another page, the resource will already live in the cache. With a lot of CDNs, developers are free to choose a CDN they prefer. Either for ideological reasons or simply because a certain CDN is the one they always use or get recommended. But when developers have a lot of different CDNs to choose from the variety of locations for the same resource diminishes the optimization they have to offer, because the same resource will be downloaded once for every url. For example; When web page A links to resource X on CDN 1 and web page B links to resource X on CDN 2, the exact same resource will be downloaded twice. 

Use cases:
> A site requires a resource as fast as possible so it can provide the best UX but doesn't care from what CDN it is downloaded or if it can be served from cache.
- A mechanism is in place to keep track of locations of identical resources.
- When a resource is required by a web page and an identical resource is already in the browser cache, that resource is used.

> Clients want to manage storage and bandwidth as efficient as possible.
- When a resource is requested, and an identical resource is already present on the filesystem, it is not downloaded again to preserve space and bandwidth.

> When a resource can't be downloaded for whatever reason from the specified resource location, an alternative resource location can be used.

~~closes #6333~~
